# eMicro CPU control-plane agent

`driver.py` is the collected JSON entry point: it reads one request object from
stdin, validates the envelope and every job, replays each structurally valid job
and streams one response object to stdout before exiting 0.

Layout:

* `syntax.py` – policy tokenizer, recursive-descent parser and every declared
  per-string bound (nesting depth, path length, complex-rule/atom budgets,
  distinct non-`match` atoms, occurrence budgets).  It also produces the atom
  and path-service counters that feed the whole-request budgets.  No predicate
  evaluation happens here.
* `compiler/compiler.py` – serial policy reduction.  Atoms become small
  complete DFAs; the rule expression is hash-consed into negation-normal-form
  residual expressions; Brzozowski-style derivatives are explored breadth
  first, dead residuals are contracted, the machine is minimised by partition
  refinement and the surviving residuals are renumbered by breadth-first
  discovery from `START` in increasing service-label order.  `DENY` (4294967295)
  replaces every transition into the removed dead residual.
* `ebpf/create_dfa.py` – glue between the parser and the reducer: it checks the
  registry and returns the canonical image (rows, accept flags, live cell count).
* `ebpf/helper.py` – `MemoryMap` is the CPU memory backend holding one immutable
  image's cells; `Agent` implements the whole versioned lifecycle (stage /
  commit / retire, spawn / clone / exit, begin / finish, open / send / recv /
  close, store / load / unlink, inspect) with exact reference, capacity and
  high-water accounting.  Every precondition is checked before any mutation, so
  a rejection is always a no-op.

Determinism: no threads, no subprocesses, no sockets, no filesystem writes and
no dependency on hash order, so repeated runs on the same input are byte
identical.  Only the Python standard library is used at runtime.
EOF
